name: mastodon-posts-scraper
title: Mastodon Posts Scraper: Hashtags, Profiles and Servers
description: Collect public Mastodon posts by hashtag, from public profiles or from the local timeline of any server: text, links, media, counts, tags, mentions and public author details. Pay per post.
readme:
# Mastodon Posts Scraper Collect public Mastodon posts by hashtag, from public profiles, or from the local timeline of a server. Each row is one post with its text, links, media, counts, hashtags, mentions and the public details of its author. You pay per post delivered. The data comes from the public API that [Mastodon](https://joinmastodon.org/) servers such as [mastodon.social](https://mastodon.social/) offer for their public posts. No account, no login and no API key are needed. Only public posts are read. Direct messages, followers-only posts and private profile data are not available and are not collected. ## What you get For each post the actor returns one row with: - `id`, `url`, `uri`: the post id on the server it was read from, its web address, and its global address (the same on every server) - `created_at`, `edited_at`: times in UTC (`edited_at` is null when the post was never edited) - `content`, `content_text`: the post body as HTML and as plain text - `spoiler_text`, `sensitive`, `language`, `visibility`: content warning, sensitive flag, language code, and visibility (always `public`) - `replies_count`, `reblogs_count`, `favourites_count`, `quotes_count`: the counts shown on the post - `tags`: hashtags in the post, with their addresses - `mentions`: accounts mentioned, with `acct` and profile address - `media_attachments`: type, address, preview address and alt text of each image, video or audio file - `card`: the link preview (address, title, description, provider, image) - `poll`: the poll summary (options with vote counts, total votes, expiry) - `is_reblog`, `reblog`: for a boost, the post that was boosted - `in_reply_to_id`, `in_reply_to_account_id`: the post and account this one replies to - `account_id`, `account_username`, `account_acct`, `account_display_name`, `account_url`, `account_avatar`, `account_header`, `account_note` (profile text as plain text) - `account_followers_count`, `account_following_count`, `account_statuses_count`, `account_bot`, `account_locked`, `account_group`, `account_created_at`, `account_last_status_at`, `account_fields` (the public profile fields) - `sourceInstance`, `sourceType`, `sourceTag`, `sourceAccount`, `scrapedAt`: where the row was read from and when A value the server does not show is null. Lists with nothing in them are empty. ## Typical uses - Follow what people say about a topic, a product or an event - Count posts, boosts and likes per hashtag over time - Build a list of active accounts around a topic, with their public profile text and follower counts - Archive the public posts of a profile - Feed a dashboard, a spreadsheet or a language model with fresh public text ## Pricing You pay per post delivered, plus a small fee for each run. | Event | Name | Price | |---|---|---| | Run start (charged once, together with the first delivered row) | `actor-start` | $0.001 per run | | One post row | `post-result` | $0.001 per post ($1.00 per 1,000) | A run that finds nothing is not charged. If you set a maximum cost for the run, the actor stops cleanly once the next row would go over it. **New to Apify?** Every account gets a $5 free monthly platform credit, enough for a first test run before you pay anything. ## Input | Field | Type | Default | Description | |---|---|---|---| | `hashtags` | list | empty | Hashtags without the # sign, for example `marketing` or `python` | | `instances` | list | `mastodon.social` | Servers to read the hashtags from. Every hashtag is read on every server. Names only, for example `fosstodon.org` | | `accounts` | list | empty | Public profiles as `@user@mastodon.social` or a profile address such as `https://mastodon.social/@user`. A name without a server uses the first server in `instances` | | `includeLocalTimeline` | yes/no | no | Also read the public local timeline of each server | | `maxPostsPerSource` | number | 100 | Maximum posts for each hashtag on each server, each profile and each local timeline. Up to 5,000 | | `onlyOriginal` | yes/no | no | Leave out boosts | | `language` | list | empty | Keep only these languages, for example `en` or `de`. Posts without a language tag are left out when this is set | With no hashtag, profile or local timeline given, the actor reads the hashtag `marketing` on `mastodon.social` (40 posts) as a sample. A run can read up to 40 sources (hashtags times servers, plus profiles, plus local timelines). Example: two hashtags, 60 posts each ```json { "hashtags": ["marketing", "python"], "instances": ["mastodon.social"], "maxPostsPerSource": 60 } ``` Example: public profile and one server's local timeline ```json { "accounts": ["@example_user@mastodon.example"], "includeLocalTimeline": true, "instances": ["fosstodon.org"], "maxPostsPerSource": 50, "onlyOriginal": true, "language": ["en"] } ``` How it works: the actor reads each source page by page (40 posts per page), newest first, and takes turns between sources. The same post that shows up twice (for example on two servers) is delivered once. Servers limit how often they can be asked. The actor reads the limits the server reports and waits for the window to reset before it continues. ## Output sample ```json { "id": "117569101702930712", "url": "https://example.com/2026/11/06/brand-guide/", "uri": "https://example.com/?p=339", "created_at": "2026-11-06T10:47:31.000Z", "edited_at": "2026-11-06T10:58:26.000Z", "content": "

A Brand Guide

...", "content_text": "A Brand Guide\n\nA strong brand starts with ...", "spoiler_text": null, "sensitive": false, "language": "en", "visibility": "public", "replies_count": 0, "reblogs_count": 2, "favourites_count": 5, "tags": [{"name": "marketing", "url": "https://mastodon.social/tags/marketing"}], "mentions": [], "media_attachments": [{"id": "117569140522189719", "type": "image", "url": "https://files.mastodon.social/.../original/f0b5b2365b4d8799.jpg", "preview_url": "https://files.mastodon.social/.../small/f0b5b2365b4d8799.jpg", "remote_url": null, "description": null}], "card": {"url": "https://example.com/", "title": "Example", "description": "...", "type": "link", "provider_name": "Example", "author_name": null, "image": null}, "poll": null, "is_reblog": false, "reblog": null, "in_reply_to_id": null, "in_reply_to_account_id": null, "account_acct": "example_user@mastodon.example", "account_display_name": "Example", "account_followers_count": 2, "account_bot": false, "account_note": "Expert services for ...", "account_fields": [{"name": "Powered by", "value": "WordPress", "verified_at": null}], "sourceInstance": "mastodon.social", "sourceType": "tag", "sourceTag": "marketing", "sourceAccount": null, "scrapedAt": "2026-11-09T12:00:00Z" } ``` ## Limitations - Only public posts. Posts that are unlisted, followers-only or direct are not collected, even when a server lists them. - Some servers hide their public posts from visitors who are not logged in. Those sources are skipped, and the run status says so. - A hashtag timeline on a server shows the posts that server knows about. It is not every post on the network. Read the same hashtag on several servers to widen the view. - Counts are the values the server reports at the time of the run. Servers differ in what they report, so some fields can be null. - The search function of Mastodon needs a login and is not used. ## FAQ **Do I need a Mastodon account or an API key?** No. The actor reads the public timelines that servers show to anyone. **Can I read private or followers-only posts?** No. Only public posts are collected, and the public profile details that the server shows with them. **Which servers work?** Any server that offers the public Mastodon API for its hashtag and profile timelines. Enter the server name, for example `mastodon.social`. Only https addresses of servers are accepted. **Why do I get fewer posts than I asked for?** The hashtag or profile held fewer public posts, a language filter removed some, or the run reached the page limit for one source. The run status tells how many posts were delivered and how many were skipped by a filter. **Does it collect email addresses or messages?** No. Direct messages and email addresses are not part of the public data. The profile text and profile fields appear as the author wrote them for the public. **What happens when a server asks to slow down?** The actor waits for the time the server reports and then continues. If the wait would be longer than a few minutes, it stops and keeps what it has delivered. **How do I limit cost?** Set `maxPostsPerSource` and the maximum cost for the run. The actor stops cleanly when the next row would go over the limit. ## Use with AI agents (MCP) Connect this actor to any MCP-compatible AI client, such as Claude Desktop, Cursor, VS Code, LangChain or LlamaIndex. **MCP server URL:** ``` https://mcp.apify.com?tools=nanodata/mastodon-posts-scraper ``` **Example prompt once connected:** > "Use `mastodon-posts-scraper` to collect 30 recent public posts with the hashtag opensource from mastodon.social. Return results as a table." ## Related Actors - [Bluesky Profiles and Posts Scraper](https://apify.com/nanodata/bluesky-profiles-posts-scraper): Find Bluesky profiles by keyword and collect posts from any profile. - [Threads Scraper: Search Posts & Profiles, No Login](https://apify.com/santamaria-automations/threads-search-scraper): Search Threads posts by keyword or download any public profile's posts: text, author, likes, replies, reposts and time. - [Reddit Scraper - $0.75/1k](https://apify.com/santamaria-automations/reddit-scraper): Scrape Reddit posts and comments from any subreddit, search query, or user profile. ## Support Found a problem or need a field added? Open an issue on the [Issues tab](https://apify.com/nanodata/mastodon-posts-scraper/issues). We usually reply within one business day. You can also email contact@nanoscrape.com.
